deep.reconstruction:
Context: Göttingen magnetometer work, c. 1837 (the next page is dated 1837 May 12). The problem is how to move a damped oscillating needle to a new equilibrium so that it arrives there at rest, without any residual swinging ("ruhige Hinüberführung").

Notation on the page:
- T is the Schwingungsdauer, i.e. Gauss's half-period (time from one turning point to the next).
- R is a quadrant, so P = 2R t/T is the phase angle ωt elapsed in time t; Q = 2R t'/T is the same for t'. The transcription wrongly has t in Q.
- P and Q are measured in quadrants. λ is half the Briggsian logarithmic decrement per swing, so per quadrant the amplitude changes by the factor 10^(-λ).
- Hence log10 p = -λP is the amplitude decay over time t, and log10 q = +λQ is the growth when the motion over t' is run backwards.

Phase-plane model (my reconstruction). In suitably scaled phase coordinates, motion about a centre c is z - c = (z0 - c)·e^{(-γ+iω)τ}, a logarithmic spiral.
- Step 1: start at rest at 0 and shift the equilibrium to the target position 1 (switch on the deflecting force) for time t. The state becomes z = 1 - p e^{iP}.
- Step 2: switch the force off (centre back at 0) for time t'. The needle must then be exactly at rest at 1. Running backwards from 1 about centre 0 gives z = q e^{-iQ}.
- Step 3: switch the force on permanently; the needle stays at rest.

Matching the two states gives 1 - p e^{iP} = q e^{-iQ}, i.e. Gauss's pair
  p cos P + q cos Q = 1,  p sin P = q sin Q.
Geometrically this is a triangle with sides 1, p, q. The angle P lies between sides 1 and p, and the angle Q between sides 1 and q (the sketch).

Law of cosines:
- cos P = (1 + p² - q²)/(2p)
- cos Q = (1 + q² - p²)/(2q)
- third angle π - P - Q: (p² + q² - 1)/(2pq) = cos(π - P - Q) = -cos(P+Q).

Together with p = 10^(-λP) and q = 10^(λQ), this is a transcendental system. The previous page reduces it to one equation in P via q² = 1 - 2p cos P + p² and Q = arctan(p sin P/(1 - p cos P)).

Numerical case: 2λ = 0.08100, λ = 0.04050. The page uses the already-found solution P = 0.73554 quadrant and Q = 0.59878 quadrant, and verifies it by logarithms.
- log p = -0.0405·0.73554 = 9.97021-10.
- log q = 0.0405·0.59878 = 0.02425.
- log p² = 9.94042, log q² = 0.04850.
- Gaussian subtraction logarithm 0.65694 gives log(q² - p²) = 9.39156, i.e. q² - p² ≈ 0.2464.
- log(1 - q² + p²) = -0.12284 = 9.87716.
- log 2p = 0.27124, so log cos P = 9.60592, cos P ≈ 0.4036, P ≈ 66.20° = 0.7355 R.
- log(1 + q² - p²) = 0.09564 and log 2q = 0.32528, so log cos Q = 9.67036, cos Q ≈ 0.5893, Q ≈ 53.89° = 0.5988 R.

Conversion to times with T = 41.6 s:
- t = P·T/2 = 0.73554·20.8 = 15.30 s.
- t' = Q·T/2 = 12.45 s.
- These are re-expressed as 38.25 and 31.12 units of 0.4 s. These are presumably beats ('P') of a chronometer beating 0.4 s; this reading of the units is my inference.

Check on the undamped limit: λ = 0 gives p = q = 1 and P = Q = 2/3 quadrant (60°), i.e. t = t' = T/3. This is exactly the first row of the table on the next page (0.66667, 0.66667). That page tabulates P and Q against 2λ; at 2λ = 0.081, interpolating 0.70913/0.75171 and 0.62458/0.58312 gives ≈ 0.7355 and 0.5988, matching this page.
errors: The marginal formula cos(P±Q) = (pp+qq-1)/(2pq) has the wrong sign for P+Q: from the triangle, cos(P+Q) = (1-pp-qq)/(2pq) (numerically -0.5013). The right-hand side is correct as cos of the third angle π-P-Q.

Small logarithmic rounding: log(qq-pp) is more precisely ≈ 9.39150-9.39153 rather than 9.39156. The consequences are tiny: recomputed P ≈ 0.73551 R and Q ≈ 0.59882 R versus Gauss's 0.73554 and 0.59878. These differences are within table precision; Gauss's P and Q come from the solved transcendental equation and the page is a check.

On the previous page the reduced equation has λ/R on the right. With the arctan in radians and R = π/2 one obtains 2λ/R (since log q² = 2λQ). This is either a factor-of-2 slip or a different convention for the arc; I cannot tell which from the page.

results.what: Two-switch (on–off–on) timing scheme that brings a damped oscillator (magnetometer needle) from rest at one equilibrium to rest at a new equilibrium with no residual oscillation. Switching times come from a triangle with sides 1, p = e^{-γt}, q = e^{γt'}.
results.modern_name: Dead-beat / bang-bang open-loop positioning; input shaping (Posicast control) for a damped second-order system
results.usually_credited_to: O. J. M. Smith (Posicast, 1957); later input-shaping literature (Singer & Seering 1990)

results.what: Phase-plane / logarithmic-spiral representation of damped oscillation, giving the closure conditions p cos P + q cos Q = 1 and p sin P = q sin Q, solved via the law of cosines
results.modern_name: Complex-exponential (phasor) solution of the damped harmonic oscillator; phase-plane analysis

results.what: Undamped limit: switch on for T/3, off for T/3, then on again (60°–60° equilateral triangle)
results.modern_name: Classical Posicast-type timing for an undamped oscillator
results.usually_credited_to: Smith 1957 (control); damping practice of Gauss–Weber magnetometry is known in general

results.what: Logarithmic computation including a Gaussian subtraction logarithm

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss and Weber are known to have dealt with calming magnetometer needles (Beruhigung, damping, timed applications of a deflecting bar) in the Magnetischer Verein era. An exact switching-time solution for transferring a damped oscillator to rest at a new equilibrium, with a tabulation against the decrement, anticipates the Posicast / input-shaping idea of the 20th century. It is an applied, instrument-practical result, and similar procedures may appear in the 'Resultate' or Weber's papers, so it is notable but not major.

checkable.asserts: Gauss's values satisfy both closure equations to about 1e-4

checkable.sympy: p,q,P,Q=symbols('p q P Q',positive=True); simplify(((1+p**2-q**2)/(2*p)).subs(q, sqrt(1-2*p*cos(P)+p**2)) - cos(P))
checkable.asserts: Law-of-cosines expression for cos P follows from the triangle closure
t ≈ 15.30 s and t' ≈ 12.45 s; in 0.4 s units 38.25 and 31.12
Undamped case gives P = Q = pi/3, i.e. 2/3 quadrant, matching the table row 2λ=0

transcription_corrections: The marginal formula reads cos(P±Q) = (pp+qq-1)/(2pq) (sign ambiguous in the hand); it is valid for cos(π-P-Q).
The first P on the page is written over or corrected (crossed glyph), as is the P in the result line.
Numbers in the result lines: P = 0^R.73554, t = 15''.30 = 38^P.25; Q = 0^R.59878, t' = 12''.45 = 31^P.12 (second time is t', not t).
'für T = 41''.6' is a heading for the time conversion column.
